title: Creatinine Clearance by Cockcroft-Gault, Age ≥16 Years

content.equation:
Creatinine Clearance Estimate by Cockcroft-Gault Equation in Adults and Older Adolescents (Age ≥16 Years) (Conventional and SI Units)
Estimated_creatinine_clearance = Sex * ((140 - Age) / (Serum_creatinine)) * (Weight†/ 72)
notes: The Cockcroft-Gault (C-G) equation was developed prior to the availability of standardized creatinine assays.[1] It has been replaced by more accurate methods of estimating GFR and should not be used to evaluate GFR or stage kidney disease.

C-G equation estimates of creatinine clearance (CrCl) have remained in use for adjusting medication doses in patients with reduced kidney function based on published sources, including regulatory drug labels. However, there is no version of the C-G equation that has been adjusted for use with contemporary creatinine values, and its use with current values can overestimate kidney function, which could lead to inaccuracies in drug dosing.[2,3]

For drug dosing, many experts and professional societies recommend the use of more accurate and equitable kidney function estimations (ie, race-free eGFR equations such as the 2021 CKD-EPI equation).[3-5] The US Food and Drug Administration now recommends using an eGFR estimate such as the 2021 CKD-EPI equation for pharmacokinetic studies and dosing recommendations rather than C-G.[6]

Calculators to estimate eGFR using the race-free CKD-EPI equations with creatinine (eGFRcr), creatinine and cystatin C combined (eGFRcr-cys), and cystatin C only (eGFRcys) are available separately. Additional GFR estimation methods are discussed in the appropriate literature as well as UpToDate topics on the assessment of kidney function. well as UpToDate topics on the assessment of kidney function.

BMI: body mass index; CKD-EPI: Chronic Kidney Disease Epidemiology Collaboration; eGFRcr: estimated glomerular filtration rate using creatinine; eGFRcr-cys: estimated glomerular filtration rate using creatinine and cystatin C combined; eGFRcys: estimated glomerular filtration rate using cystatin C; GFR: glomerular filtration rate.

† Weight: Modifications of actual (total) body weight (eg, adjusted body weight, ideal body weight, or lean body weight) have been proposed to better quantify creatinine-producing muscle mass in patients with a high BMI. However, the use of body weight adjustment(s) is not standardized or universally accepted.[3]

references.text: 1. Cockcroft DW, Gault MH. Prediction of creatinine clearance from serum creatinine. Nephron. 1976;16(1):31-41.[PubMed 1244564]

2. Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) CKD Work Group. KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease. Kidney Int. 2024;105(4S):S117-S314. doi:10.1016/j.kint.2023.10.018[PubMed 38490803]

3. St Peter WL, Bzowyckyj AS, Anderson-Haag T, et al. National Kidney Foundation Workgroup for Implementation of Race-Free eGFR-Based Medication-Related Decisions. Moving forward from Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance to race-free estimated glomerular filtration rate to improve medication-related decision-making in adults across healthcare settings: a consensus of the National Kidney Foundation Workgroup for Implementation of Race-Free eGFR-Based Medication-Related Decisions. Am J Health Syst Pharm. 2025;82(12):644-659.[PubMed 39552516]

4. National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases. Determining drug dosing in adults with chronic kidney disease. https://www.niddk.nih.gov/research-funding/research- programs/kidney-clinical-research-epidemiology/laboratory/ckd-drug-dosing-providers. Accessed July 10, 2025.
5. National Kidney Foundation. Cockcroft-Gault formula. https://www.kidney.org/professionals/gfr_calculatorCoc. Accessed July 10, 2025.

6. US Department of Health and Human Services, US Food and Drug Administration, Center for Drug Evaluation and Research. Pharmacokinetics in patients with impaired renal function—study design, data analysis, and impact on dosing. https://www.fda.gov/media/78573/download.
